citeAs: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao (2025). RoboFAC: A Comprehensive Framework for Robotic Failure Analysis and Correction. arXiv:2505.12224.
creator: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Xiamen University, Harbin Institute of Technology Shenzhen)
description: RoboFAC dataset is a large-scale and diverse dataset for question-answering on robot failure videos, comprising 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 78,623 QA pairs across 16 diverse tasks and 53 scenes in both simulation and real-world environments. It covers six types of robotic failures across three hierarchical levels (task planning, motion planning, and execution control), with eight question types targeting task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction. The dataset includes 14 simulated tasks and 6 real-world tasks, with variations in backgrounds and camera viewpoints to promote visual diversity.
name: RoboFAC dataset
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All outputs from GPT-4o used for annotation were manually reviewed and corrected to ensure annotation quality. For evaluation, GPT-4 was used as a scoring agent across three dimensions (correctness, relevance, completeness), each rated on a 1–5 scale, with temperature set to 0.2 and Top-P of 1.0 to ensure fairness and consistency in scoring.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Raw data was annotated to construct video-based QA samples for eight question types. For each question type, five question templates were provided and one was randomly sampled per QA pair. For five question types (task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, and failure locating), reference answers were directly extracted from the textual description associated with the video. For the remaining three types (failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction), GPT-4o was used with both the video and its corresponding textual description as inputs to generate reference answers. All GPT-4o outputs were manually reviewed and corrected to ensure annotation quality.
rai:dataBiases: To prevent models from overfitting to failure patterns, the dataset also includes successful trajectories (1,160 from simulation and 122 from real-world). The dataset introduces variations in backgrounds and camera viewpoints to enhance visual diversity and facilitate development of models with better visual generalization capabilities. The dataset covers tasks of varying complexity (short-horizon, medium-horizon, long-horizon, and dynamic tasks) to avoid bias toward simple tasks.
rai:dataCollection: Simulation data was collected for 14 robotic tasks in the ManiSkill environment, augmented with objects from the YCB Object Dataset and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR. Expert policies were defined by specifying target end-effector poses for each substage, and feasible paths were generated using motion planning. Failure data was generated by replacing the expert policy with code snippets that produce erroneous trajectories at selected substages. Real-world data was collected for 6 tasks via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm. Each video was accompanied by a corresponding textual description including the substage where failure occurred, the taxonomy of failure, and a detailed textual explanation of the error.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of robotic failure and success videos recorded in simulation (ManiSkill environment) and real-world settings, each accompanied by a textual description. The dataset includes 8,960 failure trajectories and 1,160 successful trajectories from simulation, and 480 failure trajectories and 122 successful trajectories from real-world executions. For simulation, objects from the YCB Object Dataset and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR were used. Real-world data was collected using the SO-100 robotic arm via teleoperation.
rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Experiments, Software Collection
rai:dataLimitations: The current integration of the RoboFAC model into the VLA-controlled robotic system is not yet seamless. The model is applied exclusively to VLA models in this work, and more targeted correction strategies could be designed for hierarchical policies. The success rate in real-world tasks remains subject to further enhancement, largely due to the VLA model's limited ability to follow complex natural language instructions.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Manual data cleaning was performed on simulation data: since motion planning for the robotic arm occasionally failed, resulting in trajectories that did not align with the corresponding textual descriptions, thorough manual data cleaning was performed and approximately 75% of the collected data was retained.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to improve robotic failure recovery capabilities, enabling more robust and transparent deployment of vision-language models in diverse and challenging robotic manipulation scenarios. By providing a comprehensive framework for failure analysis and correction, it contributes to safer and more reliable robotic systems in real-world environments.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training and evaluating multimodal large language models on robotic failure analysis and correction tasks, including: (1) task understanding (task identification and task planning), (2) failure analysis (failure detection, identification, locating, and explanation), and (3) failure correction (high-level and low-level correction suggestions). It can also be used to benchmark models' capabilities in robotic failure video understanding and to develop external critic models for VLA-based robotic control pipelines.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o was used to generate reference answers for three question types: failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction. GPT-4o was provided with the video and its corresponding textual description as inputs, using a structured prompt that included task, subtask, error type, error stage, error detail, correction suggestion, and perturbation information.
